chapters.title: How Long, LORD?
chapters.html:
Habakkuk 1

How Long?

1The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.

2How long, LORD, shall I cry for help,
and You will not hear?
I cry out to You, "Violence!"
and You will not save.

3Why do You make me see wrongdoing,
and look on trouble?
Destruction and violence are before me;
there is strife, and contention rises up.

4So the law goes numb,
and justice never goes forth;
for the wicked hem in the righteous;
so justice goes forth crooked.

I Am Raising Up the Chaldeans

5Look among the nations, and see;
be utterly astounded;
for I am doing a deed in your days
that you would not believe if it were told.

6For I am about to raise up the Chaldeans,
that bitter and hasty nation,
who march through the breadth of the earth
to seize dwellings not their own.

7He is dreadful and fearsome;
his justice and his dignity
go forth from himself.

8His horses are swifter than leopards,
keener than wolves of the evening;
his horsemen gallop on;
his horsemen come from far away;
they fly like an eagle swooping to devour.

9They all come for violence,
the set of their faces forward;
they gather captives like sand.

10He mocks kings,
and rulers are a joke to him;
he laughs at every fortress;
he heaps up dirt and takes it.

11Then he sweeps on like the wind and passes through,
and he is guilty,
he whose strength is his god.

Too Pure to See Evil

12Are You not from ancient times,
LORD my God, my Holy One?
We shall not die.
LORD, You have set him for judgment;
Rock, You have founded him to rebuke.

13You whose eyes are too pure to see evil,
who cannot look on trouble —
why do You look on the treacherous,
and keep silent when the wicked swallows
one more in the right than he?

14You make human beings like the fish of the sea,
like creeping things with no ruler over them.

15He brings all of them up with a fishhook;
he drags them off in his dragnet
and gathers them in his net;
so he rejoices and is glad.

16So he sacrifices to his dragnet
and burns incense to his net;
for by them his portion is rich
and his food fat.

17Is he then to keep emptying his dragnet,
and slaying nations continually, without pity?

Notes

  • vv5–6 "Look among the nations… I am about to raise up the Chaldeans" — the LORD's answer: the deed He is doing is the very thing the prophet fears. Ve-hittammehu temahu, word for word be astounded, be astounded. For ba-goyim, among the nations, the Greek has you scoffers, bogedim, nearly the same letters; Paul gives the verse in that form in the synagogue at Antioch (Acts 13:41). Ha-mar ve-ha-nimhar, bitter and hasty, two words of nearly one sound. To seize dwellings not their own is Israel's own entry turned around, great and good cities that you did not build (Deuteronomy 6:10).

  • vv9–11 "the set of their faces forward… he heaps up dirt and takes it… he whose strength is his god" — megammat peneihem, the set of their faces, is found only here, and qadimah is forward or eastward. Yitqallas, mocks, the verb of the boys who mocked Elisha (2 Kings 2:23); rozenim, rulers, as in Hear, you kings; give ear, you rulers (Judges 5:3). He heaps up dirt, the siege ramp, and every wall falls. v11 is obscure: chalaf ruach va-ya'avor ve-ashem, word for word the wind sweeps on and passes through, and he is guilty. Zu kocho le-eloho, whose strength is his god: his own power is what he worships; the Greek has this is the strength to my God.

chapters.title: The Righteous Will Live by His Faithfulness
chapters.html:
Habakkuk 2

Write the Vision

1I will stand at my post
and station myself on the rampart;
I will watch to see what He will say to me,
and what I will answer to my complaint.

2The LORD answered me and said:
Write the vision;
make it plain on the tablets,
so that the one who reads it may run.

3For the vision is still for the appointed time;
it testifies of the end, and it will not lie.
If it delays, wait for it;
for it will surely come; it will not be late.

4The presumptuous one —
his soul is not upright in him;
but the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

5Moreover, wine is treacherous;
the arrogant man does not stay at home.
He opens his throat wide like Sheol,
and like death he is never satisfied;
he gathers to himself all the nations
and collects to himself all the peoples.

Five Woes

6Will not all of these take up a taunt against him,
a figure and riddles about him, and say:
Woe to him who multiplies what is not his own —
how long? —
and loads himself with pledges!

7Will not your creditors suddenly rise up,
and those who make you tremble wake up?
Then you will be spoil for them.

8Because you have plundered many nations,
all the rest of the peoples will plunder you,
for the blood of man and the violence done to the land,
to the city and all who live in it.

9Woe to him who is greedy for evil gain for his house,
to set his nest on high,
to be delivered from the hand of evil!

10You have counseled shame for your house,
cutting off many peoples,
and you sin against your own life.

11For the stone will cry out from the wall,
and the beam from the woodwork will answer it.

12Woe to him who builds a city with blood
and establishes a town with injustice!

13Is it not from the LORD of hosts
that peoples labor only for fire,
and nations weary themselves for nothing?

14For the earth will be filled
with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD,
as the waters cover the sea.

15Woe to him who makes his neighbor drink,
mixing in your venom and making him drunk,
in order to look on their nakedness!

16You are filled with shame instead of glory.
Drink, you too, and show your foreskin!
The cup in the LORD's right hand will come around to you,
and utter shame will cover your glory.

17For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you,
and the destruction of the beasts will terrify them,
for the blood of man and the violence done to the land,
to the city and all who live in it.

18What profit is a carved image,
that its maker has carved it,
a cast image, a teacher of lies?
For its maker trusts in what he has made
when he makes mute idols.

19Woe to him who says to wood, "Wake up!"
to a mute stone, "Rouse yourself!"
Can it teach?
It is overlaid with gold and silver,
and there is no breath at all inside it.

20But the LORD is in His holy temple;
silence before Him, all the earth!

Notes

  • v3 "it testifies of the end, and it will not lie… it will surely come" — yafeach… ve-lo yekhazzev, the words of the proverb, A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies (Proverbs 14:5): yafeach is breathe out, and of a witness, testify. The vision is a witness who will not lie. Bo yavo, it will surely come. The Greek has wait for him, for the one who comes will come, and Hebrews gives the verse in that form (Hebrews 10:37).

  • v4 "The presumptuous one — his soul is not upright in him; but the righteous will live by his faithfulness" — uppelah, presumptuous, is the verb of Israel at Hormah, they presumed to go up (Numbers 14:44). Emunah, faithfulness, is steadiness that holds: Moses' hands stayed steady (Exodus 17:12), and great is Your faithfulness (Lamentations 3:23). The Greek has the righteous will live by My faith, God's faithfulness, and has if he shrinks back, My soul has no pleasure in him for the first half. Paul gives the line with neither his nor My (Romans 1:17; Galatians 3:11), and Hebrews with My joined to the righteous (Hebrews 10:38).

  • v5 "wine is treacherous… He opens his throat wide like Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied" — boged, treacherous, the word of 1:13. Hirchiv ki-She'ol nafsho, word for word enlarges his throat like Sheol, as Isaiah says of Sheol itself, Sheol has opened wide its throat (Isaiah 5:14). Lo yinveh, does not stay at home, is uncertain. For wine is treacherous the Greek has the arrogant scoffer.

chapters.title: Yet I Will Exult in the LORD
chapters.html:
Habakkuk 3

Habakkuk's Prayer

1A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on Shigionoth.

2LORD, I have heard the report of You;
I fear, LORD, Your work.
In the middle of the years revive it;
in the middle of the years make it known;
in wrath remember compassion.

God Came from Teman

3God came from Teman,
the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah
His splendor covered the heavens,
and the earth was full of His praise.

4His brightness was like the light;
rays came from His hand,
and there His power was hidden.

5Before Him went plague,
and fiery bolts went out at His feet.

6He stood and measured the earth;
He looked and made the nations start;
the everlasting mountains were shattered,
the ancient hills sank low;
His ways are as of old.

7I saw the tents of Cushan in distress;
the curtains of the land of Midian trembled.

8Was it against the rivers, LORD, that You were angry?
Was Your anger against the rivers,
or Your fury against the sea,
when You rode on Your horses,
Your chariots of salvation?

9Your bow was laid bare;
the shafts were sworn by Your word. Selah
You split the earth with rivers.

10The mountains saw You and writhed;
a downpour of waters swept by;
the deep gave its voice;
it lifted its hands on high.

11Sun and moon stood still in their dwelling,
at the light of Your arrows as they went,
at the gleam of the lightning of Your spear.

12In indignation You marched through the earth;
in anger You threshed the nations.

13You went out for the salvation of Your people,
for the salvation of Your anointed.
You crushed the head of the house of the wicked,
laying bare the foundation up to the neck. Selah

14You pierced with his own shafts the head of his warriors,
who stormed out to scatter me,
exulting as if to devour the poor in secret.

15You trampled the sea with Your horses,
the foaming of many waters.

Yet I Will Exult

16I heard, and my inward parts trembled;
at the sound my lips quivered;
rot entered my bones,
and where I stand I tremble.
Yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress
to come up on the people who invade us.

17Though the fig tree does not blossom,
and there is no fruit on the vines,
though the yield of the olive fails
and the fields produce no food,
though the flock is cut off from the fold
and there is no herd in the stalls,

18yet I will exult in the LORD;
I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.

19GOD the Lord is my strength;
He makes my feet like the deer's
and makes me tread on my high places.
For the director: with my stringed instruments.

Notes

  • v1 "A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on Shigionoth" — the chapter is a psalm, with a psalm's heading, Selah three times (vv3, 9, 13), and a closing note for the musicians (v19), as in For the director: with stringed instruments (Psalm 4, title). Shigyonot is the plural of the shiggayon of Psalm 7's title, A Shiggaion of David, the only other place the word is found; what kind of song it names is not known.

  • vv8–10 "Was it against the rivers, LORD… Your chariots of salvation… The mountains saw You and writhed" — the crossings of sea and river, as the psalm asks, What ails you, sea, that you flee? Jordan, that you turn back? (Psalm 114:5), and as Asaph sang, The waters saw You, God; the waters saw You and writhed… The clouds poured out water (Psalm 77:16–17). You split the earth with rivers, as in You split open spring and torrent (Psalm 74:15). v9 is obscure: shevu'ot mattot omer is word for word oaths, shafts, word; mattot is rods, shafts or tribes (as in Micah 6:9). The Greek has You bent Your bow against scepters, says the Lord.
